nuclear.dialect.md: Dialect used to check `.nuc` files outside a project. A project names its platform and dialect in `config.nuc` (or `nuclear.toml`) and the server uses those. `base` checks only the base language.
nuclear.dialect.enum.flutter: Synapsis mobile: Flutter widgets, Dart output
nuclear.dialect.enum.base: Only the base language (syntax and reserved words), without a dialect
nuclear.dialectPaths.md: Extra directories with dialects (absolute or relative to the workspace). `<workspace>/dialects` is always searched.
nuclear.server.path.md: Path to the `nuclear-lsp` binary. Empty: the one bundled with the extension, then `nuclear-lsp` on the `PATH`.
nuclear.trace.server.desc: Traces the communication between VS Code and the Nuclear language server.
nuclear.debug.followInNuclear.desc: When a Synapsis app pauses (breakpoint, step, exception), show and highlight the .nuc line of the paused code.
nuclear.debug.explainErrors.desc: Show Dart run-time errors of a Synapsis app at their .nuc line (Problems panel) with a panel beside that explains the error, the Nuclear call stack and the original Dart error.
nuclear.workspace.welcome.desc: Show the Nuclear workspace welcome page (projects and shortcuts) when VS Code starts with no editor open. Ctrl+Alt+W opens it any time.
nuclear.buildOnSave.md: Saving a `.nuc` of a backend or web project runs `nuclear build`: the running server or page reloads by itself (uvicorn `--reload`, `node --watch`, Vite). Mobile projects hot reload on save through the Flutter session.
nuclear.ai.developerUrl.desc: Where the Nuclear Developer (the local agents) answers.
nuclear.ai.graphUrl.desc: Where the Nuclear Smart Graph answers.
nuclear.ai.ollamaUrl.desc: Where Ollama runs the local models.
nuclear.ai.models.coder.desc: The local model that writes and repairs code and tests (at most 3B parameters). Applies when the Developer is started from Settings and integrations.
nuclear.ai.models.assistant.desc: The local model that plans, reviews, documents, diagnoses and chats (at most 3B effective parameters).
nuclear.ai.models.embeddings.desc: The embeddings model of the Smart Graph's search (re-ingest after changing it).
nuclear.ai.mcpCommand.desc: The program that serves the Nuclear MCP server (an AI client starts it with no argument).
nuclear.ai.graphCommand.desc: The Smart Graph's program (serve, connect, requests, revoke).
nuclear.ai.retry.attempts.desc: Tries of a call to the local agents that fails for a passing reason (down, busy, 5xx), the first included.
nuclear.ai.retry.baseMs.desc: The ceiling of the first wait before a retry, in milliseconds; it doubles at each retry (exponential backoff with full jitter).
nuclear.ai.retry.maxMs.desc: The longest wait before a retry, in milliseconds.
nuclear.ai.claude.command.desc: Claude Code's command: the Builder's lead when Claude leads, checked before every such run.
nuclear.ai.codex.enabled.desc: Use Codex (its MCP server entry and its regular check).
nuclear.ai.opencode.enabled.desc: Use OpenCode (its MCP server entry and its regular check).
nuclear.ai.opencode.configFile.desc: OpenCode's configuration file, where the Nuclear MCP server is added.
nuclear.ai.cursor.mcpFile.desc: Cursor's MCP configuration file, where the Nuclear MCP server is added.
nuclear.ai.github.command.desc: GitHub's command line (issues imported as Builder specs), checked with `gh auth status`.
nuclear.ai.jira.site.desc: Your Jira site (https://your-team.atlassian.net): issues imported as Builder specs. The API token is kept in the secret storage.
nuclear.ai.jira.email.desc: The email of your Atlassian account (Jira).
nuclear.ai.jira.criteriaField.desc: Optional: the Jira field that holds the acceptance criteria (customfield_10050); empty: read them from the description.
nuclear.ai.watch.callTimeoutMinutes.desc: A call to the local agents that takes longer is cut and retried.
nuclear.ai.watch.stallSeconds.desc: A call is stalled (cut and retried) when, this long, the Developer does not answer or Ollama holds no model.
nuclear.ai.checkEveryMinutes.desc: How often every connection (the Developer, the Smart Graph, Ollama and its models, Claude, Codex, OpenCode, GitHub, Jira) is checked; a notification says when one stops answering (0: only before each task).
nuclear.builder.team.desc: The team of a Builder run when the project's .nuclear/builder.json names none (a team id of the squad screen; empty: the team the onboarding made).
nuclear.builder.claudeModel.desc: Claude's model when Claude leads a Builder run (today's engine; a team gives each role its own).
nuclear.builder.resumeInterrupted.desc: A Builder run the editor left half done (closed or crashed) is recovered and goes on from the step where it stopped.
nuclear.builder.minFreeMb.desc: Free disk space (the project and the temporary folder) a Builder run needs before it starts.
nuclear.builder.commandTimeoutMinutes.de: A command of the Builder (a build, the tests) that runs longer is killed with its children and the step fails.
nuclear.builder.chat.desc: Who works the Builder's chat, the general agent always under the diagram: the local Nuclear Developer (the default, free), a provider's agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode) or a provider's model through an API (its key in the vault). What it spends is confirmed like a run.
nuclear.builder.chat.kind.desc: local: the Nuclear Developer on this machine; agent: a provider's agent with its own login; api: a provider's model with a key in the vault.
nuclear.builder.chat.model.desc: The provider's model (empty: its default, for the local agents the profile's assistant model).
nuclear.spending.budgetUsd.desc: The most one Builder run may spend with every provider together, in USD (0: no limit).
nuclear.spending.confirm.desc: Before anything that can spend money with a provider (an agent or a model), ask twice: first whether to go on, then with the amount and the providers at stake.
nuclear.spending.forceConfirm.desc: Always ask both questions, even when "confirm" is off. A project forces it too with "forceConfirm": true in its .nuclear/builder.json, which wins.
nuclear.atlas.contextTokens.desc: The context window of the local models, in tokens: what Nuclear Atlas's meter measures against. The Nuclear Developer runs its models with 8192 (config/project_config.nuc numCtx).
nuclear.http.timeoutSeconds.desc: A request sent from HTTP Connections that takes longer is cancelled.
nuclear.devices.idleMinutes.desc: A Synapsis device nobody looks at (hidden or not visible) this long is stopped, to free the memory.
description: NuclearLang (.nuc) support: the Nuclear workspace (projects as tabs, tools full screen, keyboard first), language server, semantic highlighting, code metrics, the Synapsis dialects (flutter, fastapi, nestjs, react) and the Chernobyl theme
command.nuclear.workspace.action: Run an Action of the Active Project (run, debug, build, test…)
command.nuclear.workspace.addToVsCode: Add the Active Project to the VS Code Workspace
command.nuclear.monitor.open: Open Monitor (time, calls, connections and memory of each function)
command.nuclear.ai.setup: Welcome and Set-Up (every setting, step by step)
command.nuclear.workspace.openProject: Open a Project as a Tab
command.nuclear.toggleCodeMetricsForArro: Toggle code lenses for arrow functions
command.nuclear.debug.otherSide: Go to the Same Line in Nuclear / Dart
semanticTokenModifier.kind: A dialect kind in a declaration header (stateless, stateful, extension...)
color.nuclearHttpConnections.platform: HTTP Connections: a platform (backend, mobile, web) or an OpenAPI document
color.nuclearHttpConnections.project: HTTP Connections: a project and its contracts
nuclear.chat.gifs.desc: Where Nuclear Chat's GIF picker searches: the pack made for the project (nothing leaves the machine), or Tenor or Giphy after it (their key in the system keyring: *Nuclear: Nuclear Chat: Keep a GIF Service's Key*; the first search asks whether the words may leave the machine).
nuclear.chat.gifs.pack: Only the project's own pack: works without a network
nuclear.chat.gifs.tenor: The pack, then Tenor (a key in the keyring)
nuclear.chat.gifs.giphy: The pack, then Giphy (a key in the keyring)
command.nuclear.chat.gifKey: Nuclear Chat: Keep a GIF Service's Key
nuclear.language.desc: The language of what NuclearLang shows: its pages, its messages, Nuclear Chat and what the agents answer in. Command titles and these descriptions follow VS Code's own language.
nuclear.language.enum.auto: Automatic: the editor's language, else the operating system's
nuclear.notifications.desc: Which notices of the local agents pop up as VS Code notifications: every one, only a member addressing you (a direct message, a mention, an answer, a question) and work waiting for you (a gate, the QA plan, the spending), or none. The workspace column's list and the badges of the strip record them all anyway.
nuclear.notifications.all: Every notice: answers, gates, runs that passed or failed, connections
nuclear.notifications.mentions: Only what is addressed to you and what waits for you
nuclear.notifications.off: None: only the list and the badges
nuclear.toolchains.python.desc: Optional: the Python executable of the fastapi backends (…/bin/python3, python.exe). Empty: the Python included with NuclearLang, else the PATH's. Given to nuclear as NUCLEAR_PYTHON.
nuclear.toolchains.node.desc: The Node.js executable of TypeScript, NestJS and React (npm and npx next to it). Empty: NuclearLang's own (nuclear setup node), else the PATH's. Given to nuclear as NUCLEAR_NODE.
nuclear.toolchains.flutter.desc: Flutter's SDK folder or its flutter executable, required for mobile. Empty: NuclearLang's own (nuclear setup flutter), else the PATH's. Given to nuclear as FLUTTER_ROOT (and FLUTTER for an executable).
nuclear.toolchains.platforms.desc: The platforms you build (mobile, backend, web): the welcome asks only their toolchains.

codemetrics.basics.CodeLensHiddenUnder: Threshold to show code lens for code metrics
codemetrics.basics.ComplexityColorExtrem: Color for the extreme complexity level
codemetrics.basics.ComplexityColorHigh: Color for the high complexity level
codemetrics.basics.ComplexityColorLow: Color for the low complexity level
codemetrics.basics.ComplexityColorNormal: Color for the normal complexity level

codemetrics.basics.ComplexityLevelHigh: Threshold to determine high complexity level
codemetrics.basics.ComplexityLevelHighDe: Code lens message for high complexity level
codemetrics.basics.ComplexityLevelLow: Threshold to determine low complexity level
codemetrics.basics.ComplexityLevelLowDes: Code lens message for low complexity level
codemetrics.basics.ComplexityLevelNormal: Threshold to determine normal complexity level
Code lens message for normal complexity level
codemetrics.basics.ComplexityTemplate: Code lens message template {0} stands for the actual value {1} is for the complexity level description
codemetrics.basics.DecorationModeEnabled: A flag which indicates whether code metrics are shown as inline decoration
codemetrics.basics.DecorationTemplate: A flag which indicates whether code metrics are shown as inline decoration
codemetrics.basics.DiagnosticsEnabled: A flag which indicates whether code metrics are shown as diagnostics
codemetrics.basics.Exclude: Array of exclusion patterns (in glob format)
codemetrics.basics.FileSizeLimitMB: File size limit in megabytes, above this codemetrics are not going to be computed, use a negative number to allow any size
codemetrics.basics.IgnoredFunctionNames: A set of function names to ignore from calculations
codemetrics.basics.MetricsForArrowFuncti: A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for arrow functions (can also be toggled via a command)
codemetrics.basics.MetricsForClassDeclar: A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for class declarations
codemetrics.basics.MetricsForConstructor: A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for constructors
codemetrics.basics.MetricsForEnumDeclara: A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for enum declarations
codemetrics.basics.MetricsForFunctionDec: A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for function declarations
codemetrics.basics.MetricsForFunctionExp: A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for function expressions
codemetrics.basics.MetricsForMethodDecla: A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for methods declarations
codemetrics.basics.OverviewRulerModeEnab: A flag which indicates whether code metrics are shown on the overview ruler
